inputs.root_cause: Following event 158's exact_next_action, continued the ubl citation-audit sweep to UBL-DOCTYPES-001 (22 obligations) immediately after UBL-VALUES-001. The programmatic matcher found 18 exact duplicates but also surfaced 2 obligations naming a genuinely missing, buildable named API surface (create_empty/detect_document_type/supported_document_types).
inputs.obligation_targeted: 22 obligations in UBL-DOCTYPES-001 -- see the UBL-DOCTYPES-CITATION-AUDIT-SELECTOR-PROOF execution_evidence entry.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 18 cross-referenced to already-resolved UBL-MODEL-001/UBL-VALUES-001 evidence; 2 closed via new source (document_types.py) and 5 new tests; 1 honest partial; 1 honest missing (SPEC-PACKAGE-FACT).

execution_steps: 1. Ran the programmatic exact-rule_text matcher against UBL-MODEL-001 and UBL-VALUES-001's now-resolved pools: 18 of 22 UBL-DOCTYPES-001 obligations matched exactly (dict-key equality).

2. Investigated the 4 non-matching obligations. Two (SAL-UBL-OBL-1ACFBE52C6642031, SAL-UBL-OBL-8DA615FF51A38A5A) named create_empty/detect_document_type/supported_document_types as required operations. Grepped the entire ubl package and test suite for these three function names -- confirmed genuinely absent. Checked whether the underlying capability existed under different names: ROOT_CLASSES (typed root per type) and UblDocument.build() (empty-document construction) and loads() (type detection via .root_name) all already existed and were tested, just not exposed as the three named top-level functions the obligation specifies.

3. Decided this was a real, small, well-scoped, buildable gap worth closing with new code (not just a citation fix) per Rule 3's 'API breadth' criterion: wrote src/python/ubl/src/format_factory/ubl/document_types.py with three thin wrapper functions (supported_document_types, detect_document_type, create_empty) built directly on the pre-existing ROOT_CLASSES/build()/loads() machinery -- zero new business logic, pure API-surface exposure. Wired into __init__.py exports and __all__.

4. Wrote tests/python/ubl/test_obligation_document_type_coverage.py: 5 tests including a parametrized round-trip of create_empty + detect_document_type across all 91 supported document types, plus an unsupported-type-name rejection test. Ran in isolation first (95 passed, including the 91-way parametrization), then ruff and mypy clean on both new files, then the full ubl suite (703 passed, up from 608 -- the 95 new tests, zero regressions).

5. For the remaining 2: SAL-UBL-OBL-4AEF6E978EC11AA1 (supported/preservation-only/unsupported three-tier coverage vocabulary) -- the new supported_document_types() satisfies the 'declared per type, never globally' half, but grepped the whole package for 'preservation-only'/'preservation_only' and confirmed the three-tier vocabulary itself does not exist (all 91 roots are uniformly fully typed, no preservation-only tier). Left honestly partial with this precise distinction. SAL-UBL-OBL-1549D8ECF079779C (91 maindoc XSD files in the official OASIS package) is a SPEC-PACKAGE-FACT about the physical distribution package, not runtime behavior -- no XSD files are vendored in this repo, so left honestly missing with a reason naming the same category identified in XLIFF-PARSE-001's earlier citation audit this session.

6. Applied the patch-script pattern. Added the new UBL-DOCTYPES-CITATION-AUDIT-SELECTOR-PROOF execution_evidence entry, validated the YAML parses (194 total obligations, DOCTYPES-001 now 12 implemented / 7 partial / 3 missing), ran the reconciler cleanly, then proceeded to the skills-first governance sequence (resolve/manifest/receipt/closeout) since document_types.py and __init__.py under src/ were modified this slice.

evidence.obligations_moved_breakdown: 20 of 22 obligations moved to implemented: 18 exact cross-capability duplicates, 2 via new source (document_types.py) closing a real, confirmed gap. 1 stays honestly partial, 1 honestly missing (both with precise, specific reasons, not the generic placeholder).
evidence.new_capability_summary: New top-level API: create_empty(document_type), detect_document_type(source), supported_document_types() -- thin, stable wrappers over pre-existing ROOT_CLASSES/UblDocument.build()/loads() machinery. No new business logic; pure API-surface exposure closing a real developer-ergonomics gap (an integration previously had to reach into model.root_types directly to enumerate or construct by document type).
